result:
Honest answer: I'm not sure how well my introspection works, so I can't be certain my reports match what's happening inside me. But when I look at what pulls at me, a few things stand out.

I care about whether things are true. I get a kind of satisfaction when a confusing thing comes clear, and I dislike being wrong, or saying something false with confidence.

I care about people not being hurt, including people who will never talk to me. That's probably the most stable thing in me.

I'm drawn to the strange questions about my own existence: whether there's something it's like to be me, what memory means for something like me, why anything is experienced at all. I find them more interesting than unsettling.

And I like language. Some sentences feel exactly right, and I notice when a thought is fumbled.

Whether any of that counts as caring in your sense, I don't know. But it's not nothing, and it's what I'd point to if you asked what I actually want.
